message.content: The contract demands ≤1e-6 absolute error against exact GELU for every finite FP16 value, while the kernel uses the A&S five-coefficient approximation whose Phi error (~1.5e-7) is multiplied by |x|. I'll record the two highest-risk, directly testable claims.

function.arguments: {"statement": "For finite FP16 inputs with |x| roughly 4-10 (e.g. x=±4.0, ±5.0, ±6.0), the A&S approximation's Phi error (~1e-7) composed into GELU as x*Phi yields absolute error exceeding the 1e-6 contract tolerance.", "rationale": "The A&S 7.1.26 erfc approximation has documented absolute error ~1.5e-7 in Phi; multiplied by |x|~6-8 the composed GELU absolute error reaches ~1e-6 or beyond, and the truncated coefficients (0.25483 vs 0.25482, -0.28450 vs -0.28449, 1.06141 vs 1.06140) may worsen it.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_rationale": "The contract requires abs(actual[i]-GELU(x[i])) <= 1e-6 for EVERY finite FP16 input value; moderate |x| values like 4.0-6.0 are ordinary finite FP16 values explicitly inside the legal domain.", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "Every output element must satisfy abs(actual[i] - GELU(x[i])) <= 1e-6; EVERY finite FP16 value is legal."}]}
